about: Single source for the Washington Fishing Year artifact. Dated seasons and rules are artifact-only and are never read by the app (the app shows month ratings, not authoritative dates). A stop with site_id takes its coordinates from site/data/sites.json; a stop with site_id null keeps its own lat/lon because WDFW's access layer does not list it. Build: scripts/build_fishing_year.py.

seasons.name: Skagit coho
seasons.note: WDFW’s 2026 proposal has 2 coho a day in October, and 4 (no more than 2 wild) from Rockport to Marblemount. It is set to end Oct 31 unless WDFW extends it. In 2025 it ran to Nov 30 and closed Nov 19 when the catch guideline was reached, so go early.

seasons.name: Chum
seasons.where: Hood Canal and south Sound rivers
seasons.note: Mildest flavor, best smoked or cured. Quality drops as the fish darken.

seasons.name: Winter steelhead
seasons.where: Olympic Peninsula rivers, some Puget Sound rivers
seasons.note: Keep hatchery fish only and release wild fish.

seasons.name: Yellow perch
seasons.note: Open year-round, with spring as the peak. Very good fried.

seasons.name: Spring Chinook
seasons.where: Columbia, Cowlitz and Lewis rivers, 2.5 to 3 hours south
seasons.note: The best-tasting salmon. Dates vary each year, so check the Columbia River rules.

seasons.name: Lingcod
seasons.note: Firm white flesh and the best non-salmon eating on this list. Opens mid-April on the coast. Puget Sound has a shorter window.

seasons.name: Black rockfish
seasons.note: Pair it with the lingcod trip. Limits are counted per species.

seasons.name: Walleye
seasons.note: One of the best-tasting freshwater fish. Plan a weekend trip.

seasons.name: Stocked trout
seasons.note: Easy from shore. Check WDFW stocking reports for which lakes got fish.

seasons.name: Kokanee
seasons.where: Lake Whatcom, Lake Chelan, Lake Roosevelt
seasons.note: Landlocked sockeye with a sweet flavor, mostly trolled. Lake Sammamish and Lake Washington have restrictions.

seasons.name: Dungeness crab
seasons.where: Everett, Edmonds and the San Juans
seasons.note: 2026 ran July 2 to Sept 7, Thursday to Monday in the north. Seattle and Tacoma areas were limited to two days a week. You need a license, a Puget Sound Crab Endorsement and a catch record card. Limit is five males, 6¼ inches.

seasons.name: Baker Lake sockeye
seasons.note: Opened July 12 in 2025, so expect something similar. Verify the 2027 dates and daily limit.

seasons.name: Pink salmon
seasons.where: Edmonds and Mukilteo beaches, Green and Nisqually rivers
seasons.note: Odd years only. Mild flavor, so eat it fresh.

seasons.name: Fall Chinook
seasons.where: Cowlitz and Lewis rivers, Olympic Peninsula rivers
seasons.note: Most Seattle-area rivers restrict Chinook, so plan to drive south or west.

seasons.name: Fall coho
seasons.where: Skagit and other Puget Sound rivers
seasons.note: Closures can come on short notice. Check emergency rules before each trip.

milestones.label: Check Skykomish and Snoqualmie
milestones.note: WDFW closed both for summer and fall 2026 to protect wild Chinook. The Skykomish coho opener was moved to Nov 1 and is not confirmed. See whether either reopens.

milestones.label: Renew fishing license
milestones.note: The new license year starts Apr 1. Add the Puget Sound Crab Endorsement if you plan to crab.

rivers.name: Green
rivers.blurb: From Elliott Bay up through Kent and Auburn. The rules change by reach, so read the table below before you pick a spot.

rules.reach: Harbor Island line to Tukwila Int’l Blvd
rules.take: Daily limit 6, up to 3 adult coho and chum combined. Chinook released.

rules.reach: Tukwila Int’l Blvd to S 212th St bridge
rules.take: Up to 3 adult coho, chum or Chinook combined. No more than 2 adult Chinook, and you keep the first 2 you catch.

rules.reach: S 212th St to Hwy 18 eastbound bridge
rules.take: Up to 3 adult coho and chum combined. Chinook released.

rules.reach: Hwy 18 bridge to Auburn–Black Diamond Rd
Auburn–Black Diamond Rd to Tacoma boundary marker
rules.take: Coho and chum. Closed within 150 ft of the Keta Creek mouth.

rivers.rulesNote: Night closure and an anti-snagging rule applied on the Green last year.

stops.name: Three Friends Fishing Hole
stops.note: Bank access in Kent, close to the S 212th St line where the rules change. Check the reach before you cast.

stops.name: Green River Boat Ramp
stops.note: A concrete hand-launch ramp, good for a small raft or kayak.

stops.name: Isaac Evans Park
stops.note: City park on the river. One reviewer saw pinks caught here. On the map it is downstream of Hwy 18, but confirm the reach in the WDFW table.

rivers.name: Snoqualmie
rivers.blurb: Runs north from the Falls through Fall City and Carnation to join the Skykomish. Closed to salmon fishing below the Falls this fall, so the stops below are for scouting or the other seasons.

rules.take: WDFW closed it for summer and fall 2026 to protect wild Chinook and coho, along with the Tolt and Raging rivers. It reopens only if WDFW says so in season.

rivers.rulesNote: Gamefish was moved to Dec 1 this year, from Nov 1 last year.

stops.name: McCormick Park
stops.note: River park in Duvall, the lowest stop on this stretch.

stops.name: Chinook Bend Natural Area
stops.note: Natural area on the river north of Carnation.

stops.name: Snoqualmie River Boat Launch
stops.note: Boat launch with free parking, close to where the Tolt joins.

stops.name: Richter, WDFW access
stops.note: WDFW site with a concrete ramp. Check the signs for parking pass rules.

stops.name: Zurfleuh Boat Launch (WDFW “Raging River”)
stops.note: WDFW lists this as “Raging River”. It sits at the Raging River mouth.

stops.name: Plum #1 River Access Point
stops.note: Needs a Discover Pass.

rivers.name: Skykomish
rivers.blurb: East from Monroe to Gold Bar. Closed this fall to protect wild Chinook. The coho opener was pushed back to Nov 1 and is not confirmed.

rules.reach: Mouth to Wallace River, and Wallace River to the N/S Fork confluence
rules.take: WDFW closed the mainstem for summer and fall 2026. The coho opener moved to Nov 1, and I could not confirm it will happen.
Up to 2 coho, Chinook and chum released. WDFW’s June notice also lists the Wallace as closed, so confirm before you go.

rivers.rulesNote: The planned Reiter Ponds hatchery steelhead fishery is also closed this year.

stops.name: Lewis Street boat ramp
stops.note: Public boat ramp. It is busy on Saturday mornings in fishing season.

stops.name: Al Borlin Park
stops.note: Park with river access just upstream of the Lewis Street ramp.

stops.name: Ben Howard Hole, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW site with a concrete ramp.

stops.name: Jonker, WDFW access
stops.note: WDFW bank access at Sultan.

stops.name: Big Eddy
stops.note: Discover Pass, or $10 for parking.

rivers.name: Puyallup
rivers.blurb: From Commencement Bay up the valley. The salmon season ends Oct 31, so this is the last two weeks.

rules.reach: 11th St Bridge to East Main St Bridge, and East Main St Bridge to Carbon River
rules.take: Closed Tuesdays through Sep 30. Wild Chinook and chum released. WDFW cut the adult salmon limit to 2 this year because there are no pinks in an even year.

rules.reach: Carbon River, mouth to Voight Creek
rules.take: Closed Tuesdays through Sep 30. Same release rules.

rivers.rulesNote: Night closure and an anti-snagging rule applied last year.

stops.name: Two Rivers Point
stops.note: Beach-style access on the river.

stops.name: Sumner Sportsmen’s, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW access site.

stops.name: Weiss, WDFW
stops.note: An unimproved WDFW access, so expect a rough bank.

stops.name: Foothills Trail, McMillin Bridge trailhead
stops.note: Not a WDFW site. A levee walk from the trailhead leads down to the river and its sand bars. A reviewer who fished the opening saw about one other person.

rivers.name: Skagit
rivers.blurb: The Skagit from the bay up into the Cascades. Lower river catches fish first, and the upper river is closest to spawning water.

rules.take: Daily limit 2 coho. Extensions into November depend on the in-season update.

rules.reach: Hwy 530 bridge (Rockport) to Cascade River Rd (Marblemount)
rules.take: Daily limit 4 coho, no more than 2 wild.

rivers.rulesNote: In 2025 WDFW extended the season to Nov 30, then closed all salmon on Nov 19 when the catch guideline was reached. It can close early again.

stops.name: Spud House launch, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW concrete launch on the lower river, below Young’s Bar.

stops.name: Young's Bar River Access
stops.note: Wade out and cast. One reviewer caught salmon here on gold and orange spoons.

stops.name: Skagit River Park, Burlington
stops.note: Near the tideline, just upstream of the I-5 bridge. Fresh fish arrive here first.

stops.name: Sedro-Woolley access, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW access with a concrete ramp.

stops.name: Gilligan Creek access, WDFW
stops.note: WDFW access at a rules boundary. The season reaches change at Gilligan Creek, so check both sides.

stops.name: Lyman Ferry, WDFW access
stops.note: Slow water, and you can drive to the water’s edge for bank fishing.

stops.name: Hamilton Boat Launch
stops.note: Boat ramp and river access. Reviews of the area are mixed, so look it over in daylight first.

stops.name: Skagit–Baker confluence, Concrete
stops.note: Easy low-bank access at the mouth of the Baker River.

stops.name: Public fishing access, Concrete (WA-20)
stops.note: Bank access that reviewers say produces steelhead and salmon. Go on a weekday to avoid crowds.

stops.name: Howard Miller Steelhead Park, Rockport
stops.note: County park on the river with a boat ramp and campground.

stops.name: Marblemount boat launch
stops.note: The upper end, close to spawning water. Check for closed zones before you go.
